### lesson-check-1.8

[Study objective 1.8](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-8)

Which is a valid compression of 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001?

- **A.** 2001:db8::1
- **B.** 2001::db8::1
- **C.** 2001:db8:1
- **D.** 2001:db8:::1

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. 2001:db8::1**

Remove unnecessary zeros at the start of each four-digit group: 0db8 becomes db8 and 0001 becomes 1. Replace the consecutive all-zero groups with one ::. The result is 2001:db8::1; only one :: is allowed per address.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-1-9"></a>

### lesson-check-1.9

[Study objective 1.9](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-9)

Which prefix identifies IPv6 link-local unicast addresses?

- **A.** ff00::/8
- **B.** fe80::/10
- **C.** 2000::/3
- **D.** fc00::/7

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. fe80::/10**

fe80::/10 marks IPv6 link-local addresses. They work only on their local link, so routers do not forward them to another link. A device with several interfaces may also need the outgoing interface named.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-1-10"></a>

### lesson-check-1.10

[Study objective 1.10](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-10)

A client reaches 1.1.1.1 but cannot resolve example.com. What should be checked next?

- **A.** DNS configuration
- **B.** Switch root priority
- **C.** EtherChannel mode
- **D.** Fiber wavelength

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. DNS configuration**

Reaching a remote IP address shows that an IP path works for that test. Looking up a name is DNS's separate job, so check the configured DNS servers, their reachability and their answers next.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-1-11"></a>

### lesson-check-1.11

[Study objective 1.11](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-11)

Which 2.4 GHz channel set is commonly nonoverlapping with 20 MHz channels?

- **A.** 1, 2, 3
- **B.** 1, 6, 11
- **C.** 3, 6, 9
- **D.** 8, 9, 10

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. 1, 6, 11**

For common 20 MHz 2.4 GHz networks, channels 1, 6 and 11 do not overlap one another in many regions. This helps neighboring access points reuse radio spectrum; legal channels and the local environment still matter.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-1-12"></a>

### lesson-check-1.12

[Study objective 1.12](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-12)

What does a VRF isolate?

- **A.** Ethernet voltage
- **B.** IP routing tables
- **C.** DNS record types
- **D.** TCP sequence numbers

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. IP routing tables**

A VRF is a separate IP route list inside one routing device. Interfaces in different VRFs do not automatically route between one another just because they share the same hardware.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-1-13"></a>

### lesson-check-1.13

[Study objective 1.13](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-13)

Which field does a switch use to learn its dynamic MAC table?

- **A.** Destination IP
- **B.** Source MAC
- **C.** Destination TCP port
- **D.** Source IP

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. Source MAC**

When a frame arrives, the switch reads its source MAC and remembers the arrival port and VLAN. That is learning. It later uses the destination MAC to decide where to deliver a frame.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-2-1"></a>

### lesson-check-2.1

[Study objective 2.1](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-1)

Two hosts in different VLANs need which function to communicate?

- **A.** Layer 3 routing
- **B.** A larger MAC table
- **C.** A hub
- **D.** A matching hostname

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. Layer 3 routing**

VLANs create separate local Ethernet groups. A switch can deliver within one group, but moving an IP packet between their different subnets requires routing and usable gateways. Access rules can then limit that routed communication.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-2-2"></a>

### lesson-check-2.2

[Study objective 2.2](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-2)

What happens to native-VLAN traffic on a default 802.1Q Cisco trunk?

- **A.** It is always dropped
- **B.** It is sent untagged
- **C.** It uses UDP encapsulation
- **D.** It is encrypted

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. It is sent untagged**

On a typical Cisco 802.1Q trunk, frames belonging to its native VLAN travel without a VLAN tag by default. Both ends must agree which VLAN that untagged traffic belongs to. Explicit native-tagging support can change this behavior.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-2-3"></a>

### lesson-check-2.3

[Study objective 2.3](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-3)

Which discovery protocol is vendor neutral?

- **A.** CDP
- **B.** LLDP
- **C.** DTP
- **D.** PAgP

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. LLDP**

LLDP is the multi-vendor discovery standard defined by IEEE 802.1AB. CDP is Cisco's own discovery protocol. Both describe directly connected neighbors rather than proving an entire application path works.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-2-4"></a>

### lesson-check-2.4

[Study objective 2.4](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-4)

Which LACP pairing forms a bundle?

- **A.** Passive / passive
- **B.** Active / passive
- **C.** On / passive
- **D.** Auto / auto

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. Active / passive**

LACP active starts the bundle negotiation and passive responds. Active/passive can therefore form a bundle if the other link settings agree. Passive/passive leaves both sides waiting for someone else to start.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-2-5"></a>

### lesson-check-2.5

[Study objective 2.5](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-5)

Which device becomes the STP root bridge?

- **A.** Highest MAC
- **B.** Lowest bridge ID
- **C.** Highest port number
- **D.** Lowest IP

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. Lowest bridge ID**

Spanning Tree chooses the lowest bridge ID as its root reference. The configured priority is compared before the remaining identifying fields, so a lower priority value is preferred; the MAC address can break a later tie.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-2-6"></a>

### lesson-check-2.6

[Study objective 2.6](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-6)

Which AP mode supports local switching at a branch?

- **A.** Monitor
- **B.** Sniffer
- **C.** FlexConnect
- **D.** Spectrum-only

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**C. FlexConnect**

FlexConnect can put a branch client's traffic directly onto the branch's local wired VLAN. That avoids sending that locally switched data across the WAN to the controller, provided the intended branch settings and services exist.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-2-7"></a>

### lesson-check-2.7

[Study objective 2.7](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-7)

An SSID works at Layer 2 but clients get no address. Which service path should be checked?

- **A.** DHCP on the client VLAN
- **B.** STP bridge MAC only
- **C.** Console baud rate
- **D.** NTP stratum only

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. DHCP on the client VLAN**

The wireless connection can succeed while address assignment fails. Trace the client's VLAN to a working DHCP server or its configured relay, and check that the server has the correct address pool and a return path.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-2-8"></a>

### lesson-check-2.8

[Study objective 2.8](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-8)

Which protocol encrypts a remote CLI session?

- **A.** Telnet
- **B.** SSH
- **C.** TFTP
- **D.** HTTP

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. SSH**

SSH encrypts the remote text-command session and supports identity checks. It protects the session in transit; a reachable management address, correct user authentication and suitable permissions are still separate requirements.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-2-9"></a>

### lesson-check-2.9

[Study objective 2.9](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-9)

A WLAN is configured but its SSID is not advertised. Which setting should be checked first?

- **A.** WLAN enabled status
- **B.** NTP authentication
- **C.** OSPF cost
- **D.** PAT overload

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. WLAN enabled status**

A WLAN can exist in configuration while being turned off administratively. Check that it and the required related objects are enabled and assigned to the intended AP before expecting the network name to appear.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-3-1"></a>

### lesson-check-3.1

[Study objective 3.1](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-3-1)

In [110/20] on an OSPF route, what is 110?

- **A.** Hop count
- **B.** Administrative distance
- **C.** Prefix length
- **D.** Interface bandwidth

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. Administrative distance**

IOS writes the two bracketed values as [administrative distance/metric]. In [110/20], 110 ranks this route source against other sources for the same prefix; 20 is OSPF's own path cost.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-3-2"></a>

### lesson-check-3.2

[Study objective 3.2](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-3-2)

A packet matches installed /16 and /24 routes. Which route is used?

- **A.** /16 with lower AD
- **B.** /24
- **C.** Whichever was learned first
- **D.** Neither

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. /24**

Both routes match, but /24 fixes more destination bits than /16 and covers a smaller address block. The router uses that more specific installed match. Administrative distance does not override it during this packet lookup.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-3-3"></a>

### lesson-check-3.3

[Study objective 3.3](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-3-3)

What makes a static route a floating backup?

- **A.** A lower prefix length
- **B.** An AD higher than the primary route
- **C.** A multicast next hop
- **D.** A loopback source

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. An AD higher than the primary route**

A floating route has a higher administrative distance than the preferred route for the same destination block. It stays less preferred while the primary is available and can become usable after the primary route disappears.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-3-4"></a>

### lesson-check-3.4

[Study objective 3.4](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-3-4)

On a broadcast OSPF segment, which router is preferred as DR?

- **A.** Lowest router ID always
- **B.** Highest priority, then highest router ID
- **C.** Lowest interface IP always
- **D.** Newest neighbor

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. Highest priority, then highest router ID**

At a broadcast-segment election, eligible routers compare interface priority first and router ID second, preferring higher values. Priority 0 is ineligible. A later better candidate does not automatically replace an already elected DR.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-3-5"></a>

### lesson-check-3.5

[Study objective 3.5](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-3-5)

What address should clients normally use with an FHRP?

- **A.** The standby physical address
- **B.** The virtual gateway IP
- **C.** The multicast group IP
- **D.** The router ID

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. The virtual gateway IP**

Clients use the shared virtual gateway IP. The physical router serving that identity can change after a detected failure, so clients do not need to replace their gateway setting with the other router's real address.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-4-1"></a>

### lesson-check-4.1

[Study objective 4.1](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-1)

Which NAT type creates a fixed one-to-one address mapping?

- **A.** Static NAT
- **B.** DHCP
- **C.** DNS caching
- **D.** OSPF

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. Static NAT**

Static NAT pairs one chosen internal address with one fixed translated address. Unlike a dynamic pool assignment, the mapping is configured explicitly and does not wait to choose a free address from a pool.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-4-2"></a>

### lesson-check-4.2

[Study objective 4.2](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-2)

Which UDP port does NTP use?

- **A.** 53
- **B.** 67
- **C.** 123
- **D.** 161

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**C. 123**

NTP uses UDP port 123 for time synchronization. This is an application port number, not a physical socket on the device. Synchronization still needs a suitable reachable source.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-4-3"></a>

### lesson-check-4.3

[Study objective 4.3](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-3)

Which DNS record stores an IPv6 address?

- **A.** A
- **B.** MX
- **C.** AAAA
- **D.** PTR

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**C. AAAA**

An AAAA record stores an IPv6 address for a name. An A record stores an IPv4 address. DNS has separate record types because a name can have different kinds of information.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-4-4"></a>

### lesson-check-4.4

[Study objective 4.4](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-4)

Which SNMPv3 level includes authentication and encryption?

- **A.** public
- **B.** noAuthNoPriv
- **C.** authNoPriv
- **D.** authPriv

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**D. authPriv**

In authPriv, auth means messages are authenticated and Priv means their content has privacy through encryption. authNoPriv supplies authentication without that encrypted-content protection.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-4-5"></a>

### lesson-check-4.5

[Study objective 4.5](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-5)

With logging trap warnings, which severity is included?

- **A.** Debugging (7)
- **B.** Informational (6)
- **C.** Notification (5)
- **D.** Error (3)

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**D. Error (3)**

Warnings is severity 4. The threshold includes its own level and all more serious lower numbers: 0 through 4. Error is 3, so it is included; informational 6 and debugging 7 are not.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-4-6"></a>

### lesson-check-4.6

[Study objective 4.6](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-6)

Where is ip helper-address configured for a client subnet?

- **A.** The client-facing Layer 3 interface
- **B.** Every access port
- **C.** Only the DNS server
- **D.** The console line

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. The client-facing Layer 3 interface**

Put the helper on the routed gateway interface receiving the clients' local DHCP broadcasts. That interface can forward the request to the remote server and identify the client subnet. An ordinary Layer 2 access port does not perform that relay job.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-4-7"></a>

### lesson-check-4.7

[Study objective 4.7](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-7)

Which mechanism buffers traffic to smooth it to a configured rate?

- **A.** Policing
- **B.** Shaping
- **C.** ARP
- **D.** NAT

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. Shaping**

Shaping holds excess packets in a queue and sends them later at the intended rate. That smooths bursts but can add waiting time. Policing instead normally drops or relabels excess traffic rather than buffering it for later.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-4-8"></a>

### lesson-check-4.8

[Study objective 4.8](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-8)

Which VTY command restricts incoming sessions to SSH?

- **A.** login
- **B.** transport input ssh
- **C.** service password-encryption
- **D.** ip routing

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. transport input ssh**

transport input ssh restricts the configured VTY remote terminal lines to SSH transport and excludes Telnet from that list. It does not by itself create users, generate server keys or select the login database.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-4-9"></a>

### lesson-check-4.9

[Study objective 4.9](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-9)

Which statement about TFTP is correct?

- **A.** It encrypts all data
- **B.** It uses TCP 22
- **C.** It has no built-in authentication
- **D.** It requires an FTP account

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**C. It has no built-in authentication**

TFTP has no built-in username authentication or encryption. It is a simple UDP-based transfer protocol. A successful transfer therefore does not establish who was allowed to read it or that its contents were private.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-5-1"></a>

### lesson-check-5.1

[Study objective 5.1](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-1)

An unpatched software flaw is best described as what?

- **A.** A vulnerability
- **B.** An accounting record
- **C.** A guarantee of exploitation
- **D.** An availability control

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. A vulnerability**

A vulnerability is a weakness, such as an unpatched software defect. A threat could exploit that weakness; the weakness alone does not prove that an attack has already succeeded.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-5-2"></a>

### lesson-check-5.2

[Study objective 5.2](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-2)

Which behavior best addresses a suspicious request for credentials?

- **A.** Reply with the password
- **B.** Verify through a trusted independent channel
- **C.** Disable all logging
- **D.** Share a coworker’s account

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. Verify through a trusted independent channel**

Use contact details you already know are legitimate to verify the request, then follow reporting procedures. Replying to the suspicious caller or using contact details they supplied does not provide independent verification.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-5-3"></a>

### lesson-check-5.3

[Study objective 5.3](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-3)

Which statement about service password-encryption is correct?

- **A.** It encrypts SSH packets
- **B.** It is a substitute for strong secrets
- **C.** It provides reversible obfuscation for certain passwords
- **D.** It enables MFA

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**C. It provides reversible obfuscation for certain passwords**

The legacy feature disguises some stored passwords using a reversible format. Someone can undo that encoding, so it should not be treated as strong secret protection or as encryption for a management session.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-5-4"></a>

### lesson-check-5.4

[Study objective 5.4](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-4)

Which pair represents different authentication factors?

- **A.** Password and PIN
- **B.** Password and security key
- **C.** Two passwords
- **D.** Two security questions

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. Password and security key**

A password proves knowledge of a secret. A physical security key proves possession of a separate item. These are different factor categories; two passwords or a password plus PIN remain knowledge factors.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-5-5"></a>

### lesson-check-5.5

[Study objective 5.5](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-5)

Which VPN model connects two office networks through gateways?

- **A.** Site-to-site
- **B.** Local console
- **C.** DNS recursion
- **D.** Port security

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. Site-to-site**

A site-to-site VPN joins office networks through their gateways. A remote-access VPN instead connects an individual endpoint, such as a traveling employee's laptop, to an organization.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-5-6"></a>

### lesson-check-5.6

[Study objective 5.6](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-6)

What happens if a packet matches no entry in an applied ACL?

- **A.** It is permitted
- **B.** It is implicitly denied
- **C.** It is sent to DNS
- **D.** It restarts the ACL

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. It is implicitly denied**

An applied ACL is checked from top to bottom. If no written entry matches, the packet reaches the unstated final deny and is blocked. Required traffic therefore needs a matching allowance before that point.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-5-7"></a>

### lesson-check-5.7

[Study objective 5.7](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-7)

Which control helps block rogue DHCP server replies on access ports?

- **A.** DHCP snooping
- **B.** NTP
- **C.** CDP
- **D.** OSPF passive-interface

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. DHCP snooping**

DHCP snooping filters server replies arriving through untrusted client-facing paths. Only deliberately trusted server/relay paths should deliver legitimate server messages; it can also build a table of observed client assignments.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-5-8"></a>

### lesson-check-5.8

[Study objective 5.8](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-8)

Which AAA function determines whether a user may execute a command?

- **A.** Authentication
- **B.** Authorization
- **C.** Accounting
- **D.** Address resolution

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. Authorization**

Authorization decides whether an identified user may perform an action. Authentication checks identity, while accounting records activity. A successful login does not automatically permit every command.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-5-9"></a>

### lesson-check-5.9

[Study objective 5.9](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-9)

Which mechanism is associated with WPA3-Personal?

- **A.** WEP
- **B.** SAE
- **C.** Telnet
- **D.** DTP

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. SAE**

WPA3-Personal uses SAE, Simultaneous Authentication of Equals, for its password-based key exchange. It is intended to improve resistance to offline password guessing; strong credentials and correct configuration still matter.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-5-10"></a>

### lesson-check-5.10

[Study objective 5.10](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-10)

Which combination is appropriate for WPA2-Personal?

- **A.** AES-CCMP and PSK
- **B.** WEP and Telnet
- **C.** Open authentication only
- **D.** TKIP and no password

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. AES-CCMP and PSK**

WPA2-Personal uses a pre-shared key, or PSK, with AES-CCMP data protection. Enterprise 802.1X is a different authentication choice, even when the data-protection cipher is also AES-CCMP.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-6-1"></a>

### lesson-check-6.1

[Study objective 6.1](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-1)

What does idempotence mean in configuration automation?

- **A.** Every run changes every device
- **B.** Repeated application converges without unnecessary changes
- **C.** Scripts never fail
- **D.** No verification is needed

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. Repeated application converges without unnecessary changes**

An idempotent desired-state action leaves the intended state stable when repeated. For example, ensuring a hostname is R1 should not keep making new changes once it is R1. Arbitrary repeated shell commands do not automatically behave this way.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-6-2"></a>

### lesson-check-6.2

[Study objective 6.2](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-2)

What is a key controller-based networking benefit?

- **A.** Removing every data-plane device
- **B.** Centralized policy and coordinated management
- **C.** Eliminating all network failures
- **D.** Replacing IP addressing

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. Centralized policy and coordinated management**

A controller can coordinate policy and administration across many devices. Those devices still forward traffic and run software; centralized coordination does not mean every user packet must pass through the controller.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-6-3"></a>

### lesson-check-6.3

[Study objective 6.3](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-3)

Which plane performs packet forwarding?

- **A.** Management plane
- **B.** Data plane
- **C.** Accounting plane
- **D.** Application plane

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. Data plane**

The data plane is the part that forwards packets using installed forwarding information. The control plane learns or calculates that information, and the management plane supports administration and observation.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-6-4"></a>

### lesson-check-6.4

[Study objective 6.4](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-4)

Which is an example of predictive AI in network operations?

- **A.** Forecasting link congestion
- **B.** Creating a prose incident summary
- **C.** Generating a logo
- **D.** Typing a static hostname

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. Forecasting link congestion**

Forecasting congestion estimates a future condition, so it is predictive AI. Producing a new summary or configuration draft is generative AI. Either output still needs comparison with actual evidence.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-6-5"></a>

### lesson-check-6.5

[Study objective 6.5](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-5)

Which HTTP method generally makes a partial resource update?

- **A.** GET
- **B.** PATCH
- **C.** DELETE
- **D.** HEAD

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**B. PATCH**

PATCH requests a partial change to a resource. PUT generally supplies a replacement representation. Use the API's documented format and permissions; neither method name alone proves the resulting network works.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-6-6"></a>

### lesson-check-6.6

[Study objective 6.6](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-6)

Which Terraform operation previews proposed infrastructure changes?

- **A.** plan
- **B.** ping
- **C.** commit-memory
- **D.** discover

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**A. plan**

terraform plan previews proposed changes by comparing configuration, stored state and observed resources. It is a preview step; terraform apply performs the changes as a separate operation.

</details>

<a id="question-lesson-check-6-7"></a>

### lesson-check-6.7

[Study objective 6.7](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-7)

What data type is the value of "interfaces" in {"interfaces":["Gi0/0","Gi0/1"]}?

- **A.** String
- **B.** Boolean
- **C.** Array
- **D.** Number

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

**C. Array**

Square brackets identify an array, an ordered list. Here interfaces contains two text strings, Gi0/0 and Gi0/1. Braces would identify an object of named key/value pairs instead.

</details>

## Worked review checks

<a id="question-worked-check-1-1"></a>

### worked-check-1.1

[Study objective 1.1](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-1)

What destination MAC does a host use when sending IPv4 to a remote subnet?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

The host uses its local gateway's MAC address, found with ARP, the local IPv4-to-MAC lookup protocol. The outer Ethernet frame is delivered to that gateway, while the IP packet inside still names the remote host as its final destination.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-1-2"></a>

### worked-check-1.2

[Study objective 1.2](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-2)

Does private addressing alone protect inter-site traffic over an Internet replacement for an MPLS WAN?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. A private address is an addressing choice, not encrypted protection. For the Internet path, plan suitable VPN encryption, working routes in both directions, availability and rules deciding which traffic may cross.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-1-3"></a>

### worked-check-1.3

[Study objective 1.3](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-3)

Why might a copper link work at 100 Mb/s but fail at 1 Gb/s?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

100BASE-TX needs two wire pairs, while 1000BASE-T needs all four. A fault in one of the additional pairs can leave 100 Mb/s working but prevent gigabit operation. Inspect all pairs and their connector terminations before assuming an IP configuration problem.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-1-4"></a>

### worked-check-1.4

[Study objective 1.4](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-4)

Output drops increase while CRCs and collisions stay stable. What should be investigated?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Investigate too much outgoing traffic for the available link or queue. Output drops mean packets could not be sent; stable CRC and collision counters provide less support for damaged media. Compare offered traffic, link speed and queue counters during a fresh test.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-1-5"></a>

### worked-check-1.5

[Study objective 1.5](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-5)

Why can allowing only TCP 443 block a modern HTTPS client?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Some modern HTTPS uses HTTP/3 over QUIC, carried by UDP, commonly port 443. A rule permitting only TCP 443 matches a different transport and does not allow that UDP path. Permit only the intended transports explicitly.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-1-6"></a>

### worked-check-1.6

[Study objective 1.6](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-6)

What is the longest equal-subnet prefix for at least 500 traditional usable hosts per subnet of 172.16.0.0/16?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

1. Try nine host bits: 2^9 − 2 = 510 ordinary usable addresses, enough for 500. 2. Keep 32 − 9 = 23 network bits, giving /23. 3. The original /16 leaves 23 − 16 = 7 subnet bits, so there are 2^7 = 128 equal subnets. /24 would supply only 254 hosts.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-1-7"></a>

### worked-check-1.7

[Study objective 1.7](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-7)

Are 172.31.255.254 and 172.32.0.1 in the same RFC 1918 block?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. The private 172.16.0.0/12 range ends at 172.31.255.255. Therefore 172.31.255.254 is inside it and 172.32.0.1 is outside it. Outside this private block does not, by itself, establish every other allocation or usage property.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-1-8"></a>

### worked-check-1.8

[Study objective 1.8](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-8)

A client has a DHCPv6 address and DNS but no default route. What should be checked?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Check Router Advertisements, including a usable nonzero router lifetime, and whether required ICMPv6 messages are being blocked. DHCPv6 can supply the address and DNS settings without supplying the host's default-router discovery. Having an address therefore does not prove there is an exit to other networks.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-1-9"></a>

### worked-check-1.9

[Study objective 1.9](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-9)

Why is ping fe80::1 ambiguous on a router with multiple Ethernet interfaces?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

fe80::1 is local to a link, and the same written address can exist on another link. Give the outgoing interface or zone so the router knows which directly connected neighbor you mean.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-1-10"></a>

### worked-check-1.10

[Study objective 1.10](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-10)

Why can a router ping a server from its WAN IP but not its LAN IP?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

The server may have a route and permission back to the router's WAN address but not back to its LAN subnet. Check the return route and access rules for the exact LAN source. The first successful test proves a different source path.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-1-11"></a>

### worked-check-1.11

[Study objective 1.11](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-11)

Why might adding APs on the same channel fail to increase throughput?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Access points on the same channel can still compete for the same airtime rather than adding independent capacity. Review channel reuse, placement, power, clients and interference. More radios alone do not give each conversation its own channel.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-1-12"></a>

### worked-check-1.12

[Study objective 1.12](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-12)

Does a shared physical uplink remove the boundary between two virtual VLANs?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. Correct VLAN tagging can keep the groups separate over one shared physical link. Moving between their different IP subnets still needs the intended routing and access rules; sharing the cable does not remove that logical boundary.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-1-13"></a>

### worked-check-1.13

[Study objective 1.13](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-1-13)

A destination MAC is learned on the same port on which the frame arrived. What happens?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

The switch does not forward the frame back out its arrival port or flood it elsewhere. Its directory already says the receiver is on that incoming segment, so there is no need to copy it to another segment.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-2-1"></a>

### worked-check-2.1

[Study objective 2.1](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-1)

If VLAN 10 hosts reach each other but cannot reach VLAN 20, has routing already been proved?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. Hosts in VLAN 10 can communicate through local switching without using a router. For VLAN 20, separately check each host's gateway, the routing function or router subinterfaces, filters and the reply path. Local success proves only part of the design.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-2-2"></a>

### worked-check-2.2

[Study objective 2.2](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-2)

How do you add VLAN 30 to an existing allowed list without replacing VLANs 10 and 20?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Use switchport trunk allowed vlan add 30. The add keyword preserves the existing allowed entries. Also create VLAN 30 where needed and verify it is active and forwarding on both switches and every trunk along the intended path.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-2-3"></a>

### worked-check-2.3

[Study objective 2.3](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-3)

LLDP sees a neighbor but its management IP cannot be pinged. Is discovery disproved?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. LLDP messages work locally without proving the advertised management IP can be reached. Check that address's VLAN, subnet, route and security rules separately. A working neighbor advertisement and a failed IP test can both be valid observations.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-2-4"></a>

### worked-check-2.4

[Study objective 2.4](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-4)

Both endpoints use LACP passive. Why does the bundle not negotiate?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Both passive endpoints wait rather than start LACP negotiation. Make at least one side active, keep member settings compatible and verify that the intended links actually join the bundle.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-2-5"></a>

### worked-check-2.5

[Study objective 2.5](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-5)

Does PortFast disable spanning tree or make switch-to-switch loops harmless?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. PortFast speeds the transition for a genuine endpoint port; it does not disable Spanning Tree. Connecting switches in a loop through such ports can cause a temporary loop, so use the intended edge design and appropriate BPDU protection.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-2-6"></a>

### worked-check-2.6

[Study objective 2.6](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-6)

A monitor-mode AP has a reachable management IP. Should normal clients necessarily connect?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. A monitor-mode AP can be reachable for administration while intentionally not serving ordinary clients. Check its assigned mode and intended data path before treating lack of client service as an addressing failure.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-2-7"></a>

### worked-check-2.7

[Study objective 2.7](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-7)

Only one centrally switched WLAN fails DHCP. Which path should be traced?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Trace that WLAN's client VLAN from the controller's wired uplink to the address server or relay. AP management uses a separate dependency path, so a healthy management VLAN does not prove this client VLAN's DHCP service works.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-2-8"></a>

### worked-check-2.8

[Study objective 2.8](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-8)

A change works until reboot. What step may be missing?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

The active running configuration may not have been saved to startup configuration. After validating the change, save it, confirm the copy succeeds and confirm the device boots the intended configuration. Leaving configuration mode alone does not save it.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-2-9"></a>

### worked-check-2.9

[Study objective 2.9](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-2-9)

The SSID/PSK works but clients enter the wrong subnet. What relationship matters?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Check which client network is actually assigned. On Catalyst 9800, follow the WLAN-to-policy mapping, policy VLAN and AP policy tag; on AireOS, inspect the WLAN's dynamic-interface mapping. The shared password does not select the subnet by itself.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-3-1"></a>

### worked-check-3.1

[Study objective 3.1](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-3-1)

Why can a /32 local route appear beside a connected /24?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

The local /32 is for packets addressed to the router itself. The connected /24 covers the whole attached subnet for delivery to other hosts. They serve different purposes; the host-route entry does not make every device on the link a /32 host.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-3-2"></a>

### worked-check-3.2

[Study objective 3.2](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-3-2)

Installed routes are 10.0.0.0/8, 10.4.0.0/16 and 10.4.8.0/24. What best matches 10.4.9.1?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

First check which blocks contain 10.4.9.1. 10.4.8.0/24 covers only 10.4.8.x, so it does not match. The /8 and /16 do match; /16 is the more specific of those. Use 10.4.0.0/16.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-3-3"></a>

### worked-check-3.3

[Study objective 3.3](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-3-3)

Will a static route AD 5 float behind OSPF AD 110 for the same prefix?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. Lower AD is preferred, so the static route at 5 would beat OSPF at 110 for the same prefix. Choose a backup value above 110, such as 200, and verify the alternative next hop and reply path work.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-3-4"></a>

### worked-check-3.4

[Study objective 3.4](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-3-4)

Must neighbors using OSPF process 1 and 10 change those numbers to match?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. The OSPF process number names each router's local configuration. Neighbors instead need compatible link operation, area, addressing where required, timers and other adjacency settings. Their router IDs should also be unique.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-3-5"></a>

### worked-check-3.5

[Study objective 3.5](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-3-5)

Why can clients be blackholed after only the active gateway’s upstream fails?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

The router may still hold the active virtual-gateway role because its client-facing link remains healthy. Without suitable tracking and upstream routing/failure detection, it can accept clients' traffic and have nowhere useful to send it. Gateway-role availability is only the first hop.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-4-1"></a>

### worked-check-4.1

[Study objective 4.1](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-1)

A dynamic pool has ten global addresses without overload. Why might an eleventh active host fail?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Without overload, each active translated inside address uses one free global address. Ten pool addresses may therefore leave no mapping for the eleventh simultaneous host. Check actual use, then choose sufficient pool space or a suitable PAT design.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-4-2"></a>

### worked-check-4.2

[Study objective 4.2](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-2)

Can devices agree on time and all be wrong?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Yes. Devices following the same inaccurate source can agree with one another and all show the wrong time. Verify the reference source itself; synchronization is agreement with a source, not proof of that source's accuracy.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-4-3"></a>

### worked-check-4.3

[Study objective 4.3](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-3)

A hostname resolves but HTTPS times out. Is changing DNS necessarily the next step?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. First verify that DNS returned the intended address, then inspect the network route, filtering rules, transport connection and application server. Name lookup and successful HTTPS are separate steps, so a timeout does not automatically call for changing DNS.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-4-4"></a>

### worked-check-4.4

[Study objective 4.4](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-4)

Does authNoPriv hide monitored counters from traffic observers?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. authNoPriv authenticates messages without encrypting their content. Properly configured authPriv adds payload privacy. Reading auth as if it also meant encryption would combine two separate protections.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-4-5"></a>

### worked-check-4.5

[Study objective 4.5](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-5)

Which severities does logging trap notifications send?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Notifications is severity 5. A remote threshold at that level includes 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. It excludes informational 6 and debugging 7; other local or remote logging destinations can use different thresholds.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-4-6"></a>

### worked-check-4.6

[Study objective 4.6](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-6)

Does a VLAN 20 access port normally receive the helper-address command?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. The helper belongs on VLAN 20's Layer 3 gateway interface or SVI. That is the point receiving local client broadcasts and forwarding them to the remote server with the client-subnet context. An ordinary access port only places its host into the VLAN.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-4-7"></a>

### worked-check-4.7

[Study objective 4.7](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-7)

Why can shaping meet a WAN rate while increasing voice delay?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Shaping makes excess packets wait before sending them, so a smoother rate can add delay. Choose the rate, burst behavior and queue/priority design so the waiting time still suits the intended application, especially voice.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-4-8"></a>

### worked-check-4.8

[Study objective 4.8](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-8)

Old management clients use SSH successfully but a new subnet cannot. What should be inspected?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Check which source subnets the VTY access-class allows, plus routes and interface filters. If existing clients already use SSH successfully, the server keys are not the first suspect for a failure limited to one new source subnet.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-4-9"></a>

### worked-check-4.9

[Study objective 4.9](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-4-9)

Why is allowing TCP 21 alone sometimes insufficient for FTP?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

TCP 21 carries the FTP control conversation. Directory listings and file contents need a separate data connection, whose direction and port behavior depend on active/passive mode. The firewall and any translation must allow that intended data path too.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-5-1"></a>

### worked-check-5.1

[Study objective 5.1](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-1)

Does an alert about failed logins establish that guessing was prevented?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. The alert shows that suspicious attempts were noticed. To prove prevention, inspect actual login results, blocking/rate-limit behavior and any successful sessions. A detective control reporting an event is different from a preventive control stopping it.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-5-2"></a>

### worked-check-5.2

[Study objective 5.2](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-2)

What should offboarding include besides collecting a door badge?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Remove or expire the relevant accounts, VPN access, keys and active sessions as well as collecting the badge. Review shared-secret ownership and access records. Physical and logical access need separate offboarding actions.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-5-3"></a>

### worked-check-5.3

[Study objective 5.3](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-3)

Does changing an enable password to a strong secret make Telnet confidential?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. A secret improves how the credential is stored or checked, but it does not encrypt the Telnet conversation. Use an appropriate encrypted transport such as SSH to protect the session in transit.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-5-4"></a>

### worked-check-5.4

[Study objective 5.4](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-4)

Why is an unattended authenticated session risky even after an MFA login?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

MFA checked identity when the login happened. An unlocked session can remain usable by someone else afterward, without another immediate MFA prompt. Lock/end unused sessions and use suitable permissions, idle timeouts, endpoint protection and revocation.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-5-5"></a>

### worked-check-5.5

[Study objective 5.5](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-5)

The tunnel is established but encrypted-packet counters stay zero during a client test. What next?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

The peers agreed on a tunnel, but the tested client packets may not be using it. Check the client's route toward the VPN gateway and whether the source/destination match the VPN selectors or protection policy. Watch both-direction counters during the same test.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-5-6"></a>

### worked-check-5.6

[Study objective 5.6](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-6)

Will a TCP 22 deny below a broad permit for the same source subnet block SSH?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. The broad permit matches first, so processing stops before the TCP 22 deny. Put the intended specific restriction ahead of the broad allowance, then confirm the ACL's attachment, direction and test counters.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-5-7"></a>

### worked-check-5.7

[Study objective 5.7](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-7)

After DAI is enabled, static hosts fail but DHCP hosts work. What may be missing?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

The static hosts may have no DHCP-learned IP-to-MAC entries for DAI to validate. Add the appropriate verified binding or ARP ACL design for them. Do not solve the symptom by making every access port trusted.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-5-8"></a>

### worked-check-5.8

[Study objective 5.8](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-8)

A reachable AAA server rejects a user. Should local fallback be assumed to override it?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. A reachable server explicitly rejecting credentials is not the same as the server failing to answer. Inspect the configured method list and documented platform behavior; local fallback is not assumed to override a valid rejection.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-5-9"></a>

### worked-check-5.9

[Study objective 5.9](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-9)

Does disabling SSID broadcast replace WPA2/WPA3 security?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. Other wireless exchanges can reveal the network name, so suppressing its advertisement does not encrypt traffic or verify users. Use the intended WPA2/WPA3 authentication and encryption whether the SSID is visible or hidden.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-5-10"></a>

### worked-check-5.10

[Study objective 5.10](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-5-10)

A client authenticates but gets an address from the wrong subnet. Is retyping its PSK the direct fix?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. Authentication succeeded, while the wrong subnet points to the assigned client network. Trace the AP's policy tag/profile or AireOS interface mapping, then the DHCP service for that VLAN. Retyping a correct password does not repair that mapping.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-6-1"></a>

### worked-check-6.1

[Study objective 6.1](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-1)

Why is a successful API response insufficient proof of user reachability?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

An API success can mean a request was accepted or a setting changed. It does not test all dependencies needed by a user. Check the resulting device state and actual application path, including routes, filters and reply traffic.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-6-2"></a>

### worked-check-6.2

[Study objective 6.2](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-2)

Does a northbound API imply that every user packet traverses the controller?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. A northbound API connects an application with controller functions. User data follows the actual device and tunnel design, which need not pass through the controller. Configuration relationships and packet paths are different diagrams.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-6-3"></a>

### worked-check-6.3

[Study objective 6.3](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-3)

Overlay peers cannot reach one another through IP. What dependency comes first?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

First check the underlay: the IP routes, reachability and allowed transport between overlay endpoints. The logical tunnel rides over that network, so its policy cannot compensate for a broken basic path underneath it.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-6-4"></a>

### worked-check-6.4

[Study objective 6.4](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-4)

An AI command is absent from the target image’s parser. What evidence takes precedence?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Use the actual device's command help/parser, supported release documentation and verified operating state. The AI text is an unvalidated suggestion. A command absent from the target image does not become supported because the suggestion looks convincing.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-6-5"></a>

### worked-check-6.5

[Study objective 6.5](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-5)

A valid token receives 403. Is this identical to missing-token 401?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

No. A 403 normally means the requested access is forbidden under the service policy; a 401 concerns missing or invalid authentication. Check permissions, token scope and the API's specific documented response behavior.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-6-6"></a>

### worked-check-6.6

[Study objective 6.6](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-6)

Why is Terraform state sensitive even when configuration uses variables?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

State can store resolved resource attributes, including secret values. Putting a secret behind a variable name in configuration does not ensure it stays out of state. Protect the state file and its storage/access controls accordingly.

</details>

<a id="question-worked-check-6-7"></a>

### worked-check-6.7

[Study objective 6.7](LEARNING_PATH.md#objective-6-7)

In {"ports":[{"up":false}],"gateway":null}, what are the types of ports, up and gateway?

<details>
<summary>Answer and reasoning</summary>

Read the outer object first. ports is an array, marked by square brackets, containing an object. Inside that object, up is the unquoted boolean false. gateway is present with the null value, which differs from an absent field or the text "null".

</details>

## Updating the shadow copies

Run `npm run docs:sync` after reviewed source changes. `npm run docs:check` detects stale snapshots without writing them. Both formats are generated from the live curriculum; direct edits are replaced. The content digest changes only when the included assessment records change.
